references.text: The parallel text in Mark tells the same event where a man with an unclean spirit cries out in the synagogue in Capernaum.
Another account of a man with an unclean spirit who cried out loudly, showing the violent nature of demonic possession.
A similar description of a man possessed by demons who meets Jesus and cries out loudly.
The context for the event – Jesus was teaching in the synagogue in Capernaum, where this man with the unclean spirit was present.
Jesus' teaching about unclean spirits, which expands on the theme of demons and uncleanness.
People troubled by unclean spirits were brought to the apostles and healed, as a continuation of Jesus' power over unclean spirits.
Unclean spirits are mentioned as spirits of demons, shedding light on the expression 'the spirit of an unclean demon' used in Luke 4:33.
Jesus drove out many demons and did not allow them to speak, showing his authority over the unclean spirits like the one in the synagogue.
Demons also came out of many people crying out, linking to the pattern of demons shouting loudly when they meet Jesus.
